summary: Brian's core thesis: most stocks trade on a 'guess' (Wall Street's estimates) while a few trade on 'receipts' — signed multi-year contracts booked before a dollar is collected — and those receipts are the sale he is buying. Oracle (ORCL, BUY) is the centerpiece: $638B in contracted revenue (up 4x in a year), driven by a $300B OpenAI compute deal, yet the stock sits ~40-57% below its high on fears of OpenAI customer concentration and negative $24B free cash flow from the ~$55B/year data-center buildout; he argues that even stripping OpenAI out, Oracle trades below its pre-deal price, and he is accumulating slowly on weakness. Innodata (INOD, BUY) is the neutral AI data-labeling 'shovel seller' — 58% quarterly revenue growth, its largest customer falling from over half of revenue to about a third — but his highest-risk name at 46x earnings with 14% short interest, so he keeps it very small. Sterling Infrastructure (STRL, HOLD) builds data-center groundwork with a $5.5B backlog, no net debt and ~40% ROE, sold off on a margin-mix dip from an electrical-contractor acquisition that he calls a non-issue. MasTec (MTZ, CONDITIONAL_BUY) holds a record $21B grid-power backlog but carries real debt and a broken chart, so he is waiting and will start small. AppLovin (APP, HOLD) is his highest-quality name — ~80% operating margins with the SEC probe closed with no action — but the chart broke on a first-ever guidance miss, so he already owns it and will add once it bottoms.
title: This Sale Won't Last – 5 Stocks Worth Buying
